title: VPC reference patterns and TF modules — sprint notes
content:
Purpose: working notes for a compact set of VPC reference patterns and a minimal, testable Terraform module surface that our Solutions / SE teams can use to onboard customers into private (VPC / on-prem) deployments. Focus: predictable routing, least-privilege egress, upgrade-friendly topology, and clear ops runbook.

Status: early sprint draft — contains TODOs, open questions, and sample TF snippets. Goal for next sprint: convert to a formal playbook + example repo with acceptance tests.

High-level outcomes we want for a customer onboarding flow:
- Tight network isolation with a single ingress/egress control plane for platform traffic.
- Support for two deployment modes: cloud-VPC peered + managed NAT egress, and fully on‑prem air‑gapped bundle.
- Upgrade plan that guarantees no in-flight request loss for stateful inference (session tokens / KV cache).
- Terraform modules that are small and composable: network, peering/vpn, kms/hsm, dns, bastion/ops, and service-endpoints.

Reference architectures (textual sketches)
1) Hub-and-Spoke (recommended for most enterprise customers):
   - Hub VPC managed by customer (or by Redwood in dedicated scenarios) containing transit gateway/virtual-router, NATs, and logging endpoints.
   - Spoke VPC(s) host inference clusters (k8s or VM pools). Each spoke has its own private subnets for GPU nodes + one ops subnet for bastion/agents.
   - Peering/Transit: prefer Transit Gateway (cloud) or BGP over dedicated VPN for low-latency large-scale customers.
   - Egress: route through hub NAT with egress-filtering to allow only S3 endpoints, Redwood control plane endpoints, and KMS/HSM IP ranges.
   - Observability: VPC flow logs -> central logging S3 / ELK; require VPC Flow sampling 100% for first week of onboarding.

2) Single-VPC isolated (SMB customers / POC):
   - Consolidated subnets with public bastion in the mgmt-public subnet.
   - Minimal NAT for images; ephemeral egress with Least Privilege.
   - Simpler routing, but fewer resilience guarantees.

3) On‑prem / air‑gapped bundle:
   - Local private control plane (containerized) + offline installer.
   - Local package repository + signed artifacts.
   - Optional hardware HSM + internal PKI.
   - Upgrade plan must include pre-staged images and dual-rootfs / kube draining strategy.

Terraform module notes (API surface ideas)
- Module: redwood_vpc_core (creates: vpc, subnets, route_tables, nat_gateways optional)
  Inputs (minimal): name, cidr_block, public_subnet_cidrs (list), private_subnet_cidrs (list), az_count, dns_zone_id (optional)

  Outputs: vpc_id, private_subnet_ids, public_subnet_ids, main_route_table_id

- Module: redwood_tgw_attachment (wraps attachment+routes)
  Inputs: hub_tgw_id, spoke_vpc_id, spoke_subnet_ids, advertise_routes (bool)
  Behavior notes: attach -> automatically create route propagation to the spoke RTs; support aws_ec2_transit_gateway_route_table_association. Keep propagation optional to avoid accidental wide route tables.

- Module: redwood_peering_or_vpn (abstracts cloud provider differences)
  Inputs: peer_type (tgw|peer|vpn), peer_id, bgp_asn (optional), shared_key (sensitive), customer_onprem_pub_ip
  Special: create a lightweight acceptance test that attempts TCP 443 handshake from an edge test VM after apply.

- Module: redwood_kms_hsm_binding
  Inputs: alias, key_spec, key_usage, policy_document (json string)
  Outputs: kms_key_id, key_arn
  Note: allow external HSM integration via an abstracted provider config (placeholder for onprem HSM plugin).

- Module: redwood_dns (route53 or cloud-dns) with split-horizon support for on‑prem

Naming and conventions (keep stable across modules)
- Resource names: prefix with rw-<team>-<env>-<component> (e.g. rw-rdp-prod-vpc)
- Variables: avoid ambiguous names, prefer lists for subnets: private_subnets = ["10.0.1.0/24", ...]
- Outputs: always expose IDs and ARNs; do not expose secrets.

Acceptance and testing strategy
- Each module must include a terratest/inspec recipe that:
  - verifies CIDR allocation does not overlap common corp ranges (simple set of blocked ranges),
  - verifies route tables contain expected routes after attachment,
  - performs an egress check to allowed endpoints (S3, control plane) and confirms blocked endpoints fail.
- CI: run short-lifecycle apply/destroy in a sandbox account nightly (keep costs low with small AZ counts).

Onboarding checklist (customer-facing skeleton)
- Pre-call: collect customer CIDR ranges, management contact IPs, preferred peering option, KMS/HSM requirements, SOC report needs.
- Pre-provision: customer creates a hub VPC or grants cross-account role.
- During provision: run terraform plan, dry-run acceptance tests, confirm route tables and NACLs.
- Post-provision: enable flow logs and forwarding to customer logging bucket, validate SSO and RBAC mappings, run e2e inference smoke test (cold start + warm).

Sampling of commands & tests (notes)
- Net tests: curl --resolve control.redwood.example:443:<edge-ip> https://control.redwood.example:443/healthz
- KMS test: aws kms generate-data-key --key-id <key> --key-spec AES_256 --region <r>

Upgrade plan (zero or minimal downtime)
- Principle: separate control-plane upgrades (canary) from data-plane/GPU node upgrades.
- Control plane: canary release to 1 ops subnet / 5% of control plane instances with traffic diversion for 1h.
- Serving nodes: rolling upgrade with drain-first policy: cordon -> drain (wait for inflight tokens to finish or migrate) -> replace -> verify metrics. Use readiness probes that wait for KV cache sync on the replacement node.
- Rollback: maintain previous image in registry for quick rollback; terraform state must support two active sets during migration.

Runbook snippets (for SRE)
- Emergency rollback steps:
  1) Flip traffic to previous model binary or container image via routing / service mesh rule.
  2) If KV cache version mismatch occurs, restart with compatibility flag and force full cache rebuild during low-traffic window.
  3) If networking teardown occurs, detach TGW attachment and re-attach previous spoke.

Operational decisions (open items)
- Should we always require Hub VPC or allow single-vpc defaults for SMB? (tradeoff: simplicity vs future scaling)
- How to represent HSM integration in TF without leaking vendor-specific constructs? (wrap provider in an interface module?)
- Whether we provide a managed transit gateway option vs recommend customer-managed TGW for compliance.

Security & compliance notes
- Default NACLs: deny all inbound, allow established outbound.
- Egress whitelist: only allow cloud provider artifact endpoints, control plane IPs, and customer-approved telemetry endpoints.
- Audit: terraform plan outputs stored in customer audit bucket with immutable retention (if requested).

Practical implementation TODOs (short-term)
- [ ] Draft example repo with 3 sample stacks: hub+spoke, single-vpc, onprem-airgap. (owner: Alyssa)
- [ ] Create terratest suite for redwood_vpc_core (owner: Ravi)
- [ ] POC TGW-attachment module with optional route propagation toggle (owner: Morgan)
- [ ] Run a dry-run with Solutions Eng for customer ACME (ticket: Redwood-3214) scheduled week of Mar 8.

Notes to self / rough thoughts
- Keep module complexity low: default to safe choices (no public IPs on GPU nodes, single NAT per AZ optional).
- Consider a small library of Terraform workspaces per-customer to isolate state; use remote backend with state locking.
- In on‑prem airgap, prefer local containerd registry and signed artifacts with SHA verification in the installer.

Open research tasks
- Benchmark route table scale limits when using TGW + 50 spokes — what threshold forces separate TGW route tables?
- Edge-case: KMS cross-account decrypt latencies and impact on request startup for short-lived inference containers.

References / links to internal folks
- Solutions Eng: Diego Alvarez (primary SE for enterprise customers)
- Security: Priya Nair (review KMS/HSM integration and policy templates)
- Release Engineering: Samir Joshi (coordinate dual-rootfs upgrade mechanism)

End of sprint notes — aim to convert to a readable playbook and publish as /infra/examples/private-deployments in the next two sprints.
